web_evidence.title: Robert James Waller Writing Styles in The Bridges of Madison County
web_evidence.note: Detailed structural analysis explicitly identifies limited-third narration in the central story and first-person narration in both the preface and postscript; this is corroborated by an independent study guide and the section texts.

web_evidence.title: The Bridges of Madison County Chapters 1-4 Summary & Analysis
web_evidence.note: Detailed chapter analysis identifies the opening narrator as a participating researcher who meets Michael and Carolyn, then describes the following Robert and Francesca chapters through sustained external third-person narration.

web_evidence.title: The Bridges of Madison County Character Analysis
web_evidence.note: Independent structural analysis treats the narrator as a character whose research bookends the novel, corroborating that the first-person frame is repeated rather than an isolated pronoun.

web_evidence.title: The Bridges of Madison County — The Beginning
web_evidence.note: The complete opening section sustains an author-researcher voice using I and we while recounting meetings, investigation, and composition of the story.

web_evidence.title: The Bridges of Madison County — The Tacoma Nighthawk
web_evidence.note: The postscript again sustains the participating author's I-voice as he travels, researches Kincaid, locates Cummings, and introduces the interview transcript.

web_evidence.title: The Bridges of Madison County by Robert James Waller
web_evidence.note: The library record verifies the work and supplies only its first story-body sentence, which refers to Robert Kincaid externally; the passage is too short to establish whole-book structure.

Searched "The Bridges of Madison County narrative point of view third person scholarly" and "narrator point of view frame narrative analysis"; BookRags explicitly distinguished the third-person central story from first-person preface and postscript.
Opened SuperSummary's chapter and narrator analyses; they independently identified the researching narrator at both bookends and described the intervening Robert and Francesca narrative.

Searched Google Books, Open Library, and Internet Archive records; Google Books was bibliographic and Open Library exposed only one story-body sentence, so neither preview alone was treated as whole-book proof.
Searched exact section titles and opening language, then opened the full texts of "The Beginning" and "The Tacoma Nighthawk" to confirm sustained first-person narration at both ends.
Opened the full "Interview with Nighthawk Cummings" text to identify q03253, q03264, and q03279 as embedded interview material rather than evidence of the authorial frame.

A national-tour educational guide described the novel simply as third person; targeted follow-up showed that this accurately summarizes the central romance but omits the documented first-person bookends.
person_note: The central Robert–Francesca romance, which constitutes the book's base narrative, is sustained third person. The participating author-researcher appears in an opening and postscript, but those framing bookends do not override the controlling person of the main narrative. Letters, dialogue, and other embedded first-person material are also local, so the book label is THIRD.
